headline: FY2026 largely preserves Walmart's established omnichannel/AI, cyber, regulatory, and litigation risk architecture, but it sharpens the filing around AI-mediated shopping and competition, AI-amplified cyber threats, and a more immediate tariff-and-pricing pressure story.
summary: The clearest lead shift is from treating AI mainly as an internal operating tool with compliance complexity to treating AI and emerging agentic platforms as customer-facing gateways that can reshape search, discovery, advertising, purchasing, and Walmart's direct customer relationship.
card_takeaway: Best default read for the public case: it keeps Walmart calm while making the customer-interface, cyber, and tariff sharpenings explicit.
why_this_lane_matters: This is the hero lane because it best distinguishes a calm but meaningful operating shift from a full risk-map rewrite.

output_shape_info.display_text: Canonical structured brief plus evidence bundle

auditability_note: High auditability: P2 keeps the customer-interface, AI-cyber, and tariff-specific sharpenings adjacent to evidence.
strengths: Strongest separation between core reused scaffolds and the sharper agentic-commerce and tariff needles.
Keeps the case calm and selective instead of overstating change.
limitations: Still a tagged-packet comparison rather than proof of a whole-filing enterprise reprioritization.
Many changes remain better read as intensified examples inside longstanding categories.

evidence_preview.quote_text: We continue to invest in AI and generative AI technologies to enhance our customers’ shopping experience and our associate work experience and to improve efficiencies of our supply chain, operations, management functions and talent recruitment and development; however, these are evolving technologies and there are inherent operational and legal complexities associated with implementation of these technologies within our business.
evidence_preview.short_note: FY2025 baseline AI/generative AI investment and complexity framing.

evidence_preview.quote_text: When integrating and introducing AI and generative AI technologies into our platforms, processes and systems, we may be exposed to new or expanded liabilities and risks due to elevated governmental scrutiny and monitoring, litigation, data privacy risks and compliance issues in a disparate and at times conflicting regulatory environment, all of which could negatively affect our financial performance and business reputation.
evidence_preview.short_note: FY2025 baseline AI integration liability and compliance framing.

evidence_preview.quote_text: Cyberattacks and threat actors can be sponsored by particular nation-states, or be the work of sophisticated criminal organizations, insiders (including our associates or contractors) or third parties, each with a wide-range of motives and expertise.
